passage:
A power company sent families a monthly report comparing their electricity use with similar homes nearby.
Some families ignored it. Others became curious. One family noticed they used much more power than neighbors. They checked their habits and found an old refrigerator using too much electricity.
After replacing it and turning off unused devices, their bill dropped.
The report worked because it made invisible use visible. People do not usually see electricity leaving their homes. They only see the bill later.
Information can change behavior when it is clear, personal, and connected to choices people can actually make.
